paper.core_task: Referring video segmentation with motion-centric evaluation

contributions.name: A motion-centric probing and evaluation benchmark
contributions.author_claim_text: we propose a motion-centric probing and evaluation to study the shortcomings in video MLLMs with respect to capturing spatiotemporal dynamics
contributions.description: A benchmark that inserts a static keyframe into videos to test if models truly use motion information, revealing that state-of-the-art methods are biased toward static cues.

contributions.name: Strong single-image and semi-temporal baselines
contributions.author_claim_text: we propose three strong baselines that outperform the state of the art while being static biased
contributions.description: Three baselines using MLLMs (like Qwen2.5-VL) and SAM 2.0 that achieve state-of-the-art performance on standard benchmarks but rely on static information, highlighting the benchmarks' limitations.

novelty_claims.text: The paper's main contribution is the motion-centric probing and evaluation technique, but the technical novelty is limited.

The core of the method relies on manipulating existing video data by inserting keyframes, which, while effective in highlighting the limitations of current models, does not represent a significant methodological advancement.
